"Palemoon" would be what you looking for, most likely.

For sites that do expect you to run Firefox or Chrome, you do not really need to keep those around, by the way - The way those sites normally see what you are running is based on the so-called "useragent", which is just a simple string identifying your browser, and it can be set at your free choice to pretty much anything.

Assuming you run Palemoon and want to access "google plus", which will claim your browser was not supported, go to about:config and set the following (type "useragent" in the search field)

general.useragent.enable_overrides = true

general.useragent.site_specific_overrides = true

Right-click -> New -> String, name it "general.useragent.plus.google.com" -> Select and set its value to something like "Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; X11; rv:38.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/38.0" (feel free to copy-paste this). Obviously this works for any site, just add an override of the name "general.useragent.[Site.Domain.TLD]"!

You can use certain plug-ins to give you a "user-friendly" interface to do this, but in the result is the same.
